lines.text: You ask an AI chatbot a question, and it answers like a person. But it's really playing one simple game, over and over.
Guess the next word. That's it.
First, your message is chopped into small pieces called tokens. Common words are one piece. Rare words get split up.
Each token becomes a long list of numbers, an address on a giant map of meaning, where similar words sit close together.
Then, layer after layer, every word looks at every other word, to work out what matters. That trick is called attention.
At the end, every possible next word gets a score. Paris, ninety percent. London, five percent.
It picks one, adds it to the text, and runs the whole thing again. Word, by word, by word.
How did it learn? By guessing the next word across a mountain of text, and nudging billions of numbers every time it got it wrong.
That's also why it can sound sure, and still be wrong. It predicts what sounds right, not what's been checked.
So be careful what you paste in, many AI services can keep your chats. For a private file, use Orbi Transfer. Locked on your phone, gone in 30 minutes.
